Location Optional

Daily insights
Economic Times
RBI repo rate pauses: what it means for your home loan
The Reserve Bank of India has kept the repo rate unchanged at 6.5%. Existing borrowers are relieved as EMI burdens won't rise. Fixed deposit rates may have peaked.
Experts suggest this is the perfect time to lock in long-term fixed deposits before rates potentially drop next quarter. For home loan borrowers, consider prepaying principal if you have surplus funds to reduce overall interest outgo.
Mint
Index funds vs active mutual funds in 2026
With markets at all-time highs, the debate between passive index funds and active management heats up. Data shows 60% of large-cap active funds underperformed their benchmarks last year.
Investors looking for stability and lower expense ratios are heavily moving towards Nifty 50 and Sensex index funds. Active funds still hold an edge in mid and small-cap segments where stock-picking alpha remains significant.
Bloomberg
Tax-saving instruments under the new regime
The revised tax slabs under the new regime change the math on ELSS, PPF, and insurance-linked savings. Here's how to pick the right mix for your bracket.
For young earners under ₹12L income, the new regime often wins. ELSS still makes sense as a growth instrument, even without tax benefits. PPF is better viewed as a long-horizon safety asset rather than a tax shield.

About this masterclass

This live session is built for families navigating shared financial decisions — partners, parents, and adult children figuring out how to budget, plan, and grow money together.

You'll walk away with a working framework for joint accounts, shared goals, and how to handle disagreements about spending. Real examples from Indian households included.

What you'll learn
  • How to set up a shared family budget that works for everyone
  • Joint vs separate accounts: what to choose and when
  • Aligning on long-term goals: house, education, retirement
  • Talking about money without arguments — practical scripts
  • Live Q&A — bring your specific situations

Why we need your PAN
Secure credit access & insights

We request your PAN details to verify your identity and securely fetch your CIBIL score. This helps us provide accurate credit insights, loan eligibility, and personalized financial recommendations.

Your PAN information is encrypted and used only for verification and credit assessment purposes. We do not share your data with third parties without your consent, except where required by law or to retrieve your credit information from authorized credit bureaus.
